interest: This List of Papers provides a concise record of U.S. intelligence tracking of Japanese military personnel immediately preceding and following the outbreak of the Pacific War. It highlights the surveillance of Japanese command structures in occupied Shanghai in late 1941, as well as the movements of Japanese military attachés across South American nations (Bolivia, Peru, and Chile) in early 1942. For historians of World War II and intelligence, it is particularly useful for identifying diplomatic and military networks in neutral Latin American countries and following cross-references to the Confidential File and decimal file 701.9424/8.
overview: This file consists of a single-page Department of State 'List of Papers' (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, for decimal file 894.22 (misprinted as 294.22), concerning Japanese military personnel, organization, discipline, and service. The document inventories two items: Sub-number 25, a September 30, 1941 report from the Naval Attaché in Japan regarding Japanese command and staff stationed at Shanghai (cross-referenced to 894/32); and Sub-number 26, a January 21, 1942 War Department confidential report documenting the movements and accreditations of Japanese military attachés in South America, specifically Bolivia, Peru, and Chile (cross-referenced to 701.9424/8).

subfiles.summary: This document is a Department of State List of Papers (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing entries under decimal file 894.22 (Personnel. Organization. Discipline. Mutiny. Compulsory Military Service). It records Sub-number 25 (dated September 30, 1941) from the Naval Attaché concerning Japanese commanders and staff in Shanghai, and Sub-number 26 (dated January 21, 1942) from the War Department regarding Japanese military attachés operating in Bolivia, Peru, and Chile. The sheet also notes cross-references to decimal file 701.9424/8 and related confidential files.
